For instance say all the allocated shares for a company have been sold. The price of the shares fluctuates then drops all the way down to zero - like a Bill Ackman Herbalife short.

If the company is still a going concern and still has tangible assets and produces a net profit. Does the company (legal entity) really care about the share price?
What happens to a company when the stock price goes down to zero?

Share price means nothing to a company unless they are trying to raise capital. A share price of 0 doesnt really exist either. Unless you are exchanging ownership, like to a family member of something, you can't buy a share for 0. A share price of 0.00001 (number of 0s depends on the market, eg, ASX in Australia min price is $0.001), just means that the company is shit, no one wants the shares and it probably will go bankrupt eventually.

If the company is trying to get more money after their issue float, then the share price matters as this will effect the amount of money they can get per new shares issued.

Ultimately, stock shares are defined as "portions of ownership of capital". If a company is about to cease to be, then the process goes kinda like:

  • Convert company capital into money (auction office chairs, sell offices the company owned outright, etc)
  • Use the law and the company charter to begin splitting up the money:
  • Pay shareholders
  • Pay creditors

Basically, the stock price rises and falls because, at the end of the day, that stock is an estimation of how much you will get if the company just goes tits-up that particular moment.

The "value train" goes up as a company does more cool shit, and down as they fuck up, so you never ususally see high-value stocks suddenly "turn into cash".

Curiously, this means that it can be a worthwhile strategy to watch stocks that crater into the ground, and buy them up right before the company finally folds. Nobody in the stock market really wants to wait for the shit to get auction; they just want to get out. Sometimes you can turn a decent profit by buying up while it's cheap.
